case_name: Century Campus Housing Management, L.P. v. Elda Hana, LLC

issues.label: Standard for Rule 41(b) dismissal
issues.why: Court must apply the correct legal standard governing involuntary dismissal for failure to prosecute.

issues.label: Required findings of delay and prejudice
issues.why: Rule 41(b) dismissal typically requires findings on the nature of delay and prejudice to the defendant.

issues.label: Consideration of lesser sanctions
issues.why: Dismissal with prejudice is a harsh sanction requiring consideration of whether lesser alternatives suffice.

issues.label: Adequacy of trial court's stated reasons
issues.why: The minute order and written order may lack sufficient findings to support the drastic dismissal.

issues.label: Whether dismissal with prejudice was warranted
issues.why: Dismissal with prejudice bars refiling and must be justified by more than mere delay.

issues.label: Fault attributable to party vs. counsel
issues.why: Court must consider whether delay was due to the party or attorney and whether party was culpable.

issues.label: Explanation offered in opposition
issues.why: EH/KAD's opposition may provide justification for the delay that the court must weigh.

issues.label: Century's own inaction and mutual delay
issues.why: Both parties failed to advance the case, raising whether delay is fairly charged only to EH/KAD.

issues.label: Century's minimal briefing on the motion
issues.why: The movant's cursory discussion may fail to carry its burden for dismissal.

issues.label: Right to a hearing on the motion
issues.why: Deciding the motion without hearing may implicate procedural fairness or local rule requirements.

issues.label: Discrepancy between minute order and written order
issues.why: The written order references arguments of counsel and an April 17 order, creating inconsistencies about what was decided.

issues.label: Effect of prior appeal and remand
issues.why: The remand history may affect what actions were expected and the timeline for prosecution.

issues.label: Impact of pending summary judgment motions
issues.why: Century's earlier partial summary judgment motions may have affected the case's procedural posture.

issues.label: Whether COVID-19 period excuses delay
issues.why: The delay period beginning March 2020 coincides with pandemic disruptions to court operations.

issues.label: Abandonment as a distinct ground
issues.why: Century suggested abandonment, requiring analysis separate from mere failure to prosecute.

issues.label: Denial of motion for reconsideration
issues.why: Court must assess whether reconsideration was properly denied under applicable standards.

issues.label: Standard of review on appeal
issues.why: Rule 41(b) dismissals are reviewed for abuse of discretion, framing the appellate analysis.

issues.label: Pre-trial statement and court scheduling duties
issues.why: Whether the court itself failed to set deadlines or trial affects fault for inaction.

issues.label: Century's delay in submitting written order
issues.why: Century took nearly nine months to submit the proposed order, bearing on diligence expectations.

issues.label: Finality and timeliness of appeal
issues.why: Court must confirm the final judgment supports appellate jurisdiction and timing.
